newsitem.title: USA: House debates airline ticket tax extension.
newsitem.headline: House debates airline ticket tax extension.

text.p: The House Tuesday debated a bill to reimpose the 10 percent airline ticket tax but put off a roll-call vote until at least Wednesday.
The ticket tax expired Dec. 31. The bill would reinstate the tax until Sept. 30, the end of the government's fiscal year.
The bill was considered under procedures which require a two-thirds majority for passage. A similar bill is pending in the Senate.

Supporters of the bill said revenues from the tax were needed to keep the airport and airways trust fund from running out of money next month. The fund is used to pay for improvements at airports and the air traffic control system.
But opponents, led by Tennessee Republican Van Hilleary, said the bill should not be passed unless it included an offsetting tax cut.
"I think it is going to be tough for other conservative members of Congress to vote for this $2.7 billion tax increase," Hilleary said.
Several major airlines say the tax is unfair to them and have asked Congress to replace it with user fees.
